messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` is failing. It creates an ExtendedMessageFormat instance with a pattern containing single quotes and uses a custom registry. The current bug report indicates that using a custom format registry along with a pattern containing single quotes causes an OutOfMemoryError.

The constructor ExtendedMessageFormat(String pattern, Map registry) delegates to another constructor passing the default locale. That constructor stores the registry and calls applyPattern(pattern).

In applyPattern(String pattern), if the registry is not null, it processes the pattern manually instead of delegating to the superclass. It parses the pattern, recognizing quoting characters and format elements. For quoted strings (single quotes), it calls appendQuotedString.

The appendQuotedString method parses quoted substrings in the pattern and appends them to a StringBuffer. This method uses a loop to scan characters and properly handles escaped quotes ("''").

The test's pattern is `"it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!"`, which contains escaped quotes (`''`) and quoted literals (`'test'`). In appendQuotedString, when it meets escapingOn and two consecutive quotes, it appends a single quote and skips ahead.

Given the OutOfMemoryError, the likely root cause is an infinite loop or excessive processing due to incorrect handling of single quotes in conjunction with the custom format registry in applyPattern.

Specifically, the applyPattern method uses a while loop with a ParsePosition. When it encounters a quote character (case QUOTE), it calls appendQuotedString passing the original pattern and ParsePosition. If appendQuotedString doesn't correctly update the position index in all cases, the outer while loop could be stuck repeatedly processing the same quote character, causing a loop.

In appendQuotedString, the code handles escaped quotes and quoted substrings, advancing the position (pos) accordingly. However, the first if statement (line 421-423) returns immediately if escapingOn is true and the character at position is a quote, without advancing the position. This can cause applyPattern's while loop at line 155-189 to never advance the index when a quote is encountered, leading to an infinite loop and eventually an OutOfMemoryError due to unbounded memory use from the loop.

Hence, the bug arises from the interaction of applyPattern and appendQuotedString when handling patterns containing escaped quotes with a custom format registry. The failure to advance the ParsePosition index during escaped quote handling causes an infinite loop.

Recent bug reports do not provide additional relevant information.

Summary: The OutOfMemoryError occurs because appendQuotedString, when escapingOn is true and encountering a quote character (escaped quote), does not advance the parse position, causing applyPattern to loop infinitely on the same position.

Fixing this issue would require ensuring appendQuotedString always advances the position index (pos) even in the special case of escaped quotes, preventing infinite loops in applyPattern when parsing patterns with quoted literals and a custom format registry.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
